newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP says year outlook encouraging.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP says year outlook encouraging.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) said on Friday that the outlook for the rest of the year to May 31, 1997 is encouraging.
BHP said steel prices remain under pressure.
"Copper prices, however remain volatile and no definitive projections can be made of them," BHP said.
It said the group will continue to bring forward new projects to sustain its growth strategies.
"The outlook for the group for the remainder of this financial year is, overall, moderately encouraging," BHP said.
BHP reported a net profit after abnormals of A$790 million in the six months ended November 30, 1996, compared with A$876 million a year earlier.
It said across the businesses, operations were generally expected to remain at or close to capacity with no significant scheduled interruptions.
"The price outlook for our products is more mixed," it said.
"Minerals prices mostly will remain at about current levels under contracts in force until at least 1 April 1997."
"Petroleum prices have recently been at higher levels than were anticipated," BHP said.

BHP said work will continue to improve costs, capital efficiency and production yields in pursuit of higher rates of return and to continue the programme to build the group around those assets with the potential to contribute to shareholders wealth.
At noon (0100 GMT), BHP shares were 17 cents up at A$17.22. The shares were trading at A$17.45 when the results were announced at 0030 GMT.
